summaryAnalysis.cliftonContext: Parsippany-Troy Hills has a certified tax rate of 3.550% (including Fire District avg) and a 66.60% equalization ratio, yielding an effective true-market tax rate of ~2.30%. That effective rate is higher than neighboring Hanover/Whippany (1.49%), Morris Plains (1.92%), Florham Park (1.42%), and Montville (2.06%), driven by Parsippany's loss of corporate office ratables and 64.1% school tax share.
summaryAnalysis.taxBurdenDrivers: In Morris County, county taxes are remarkably low (~9.5% of the bill), while local school districts represent 60%–70% of every homeowner's property tax check.

towns.name: Parsippany-Troy Hills
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Largest township in Morris County with 14 public schools and major highway access (I-80, I-287, Rt 10, Rt 46). However, corporate office park vacancies and 30-year PILOT apartment conversions have shifted +$29.4M/yr onto residential homeowners.

towns.name: Morris Plains Borough
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Compact borough with strong commercial ratables (Honeywell HQ, Tabor Road Gables) and K-8 district sending high schoolers to Morristown High School.

towns.name: Hanover Township (Whippany / Cedar Knolls)
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Enjoys one of the lowest effective tax rates in Morris County (1.49%) thanks to strong corporate/pharma ratables (Bayer, Barclays, Wegmans corridor) and disciplined commercial retention.

towns.name: Denville Township
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Vibrant walkable downtown and lake communities (Indian Lake, Cedar Lake); funds K-8 Denville schools plus Morris Hills Regional High School.

towns.name: Montville Township
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Affluent suburban township with top-rated school district; like Parsippany, Montville also uses separate Fire Districts (Fire Districts 1–3).

towns.name: Mountain Lakes Borough
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Historic Hapgood estate community with $28,500+ average property tax bills due to nearly 100% residential tax base and minimal commercial ratables.

towns.name: Boonton Town
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Historic Main Street town; higher effective tax rate (2.384%) due to smaller geographic footprint and limited corporate office parks.

towns.name: Morristown Town
towns.strengthsAndWatchdogNotes: Booming regional downtown with surging commercial office/retail ratables (M Station / Deloitte / Sanofi), keeping Morristown's effective tax rate (1.945%) well below Parsippany's (2.302%).

comparativeKeyFindings.title: Why Hanover (1.49%) & Morristown (1.95%) Beat Parsippany's Effective Rate (2.30%)
comparativeKeyFindings.detail: Hanover Township (Whippany) and Morristown protected and modernized their commercial ratables without giving away 30-year school-exempt residential PILOTs. In contrast, Parsippany's office park conversions shifted school costs onto homeowners.

comparativeKeyFindings.title: Schools Take 64.1% of Parsippany's Tax Bill vs. 9.5% for Morris County
comparativeKeyFindings.detail: Unlike Passaic or Essex Counties where county taxes consume 18%–23% of a homeowner's bill, Morris County takes just 9.52%. However, because NJ State Aid covers under 10% of PTHSD's budget, 64.14% of every Parsippany tax dollar goes to the school district.

comparativeKeyFindings.title: The 66.6% Equalization Ratio & Upcoming Revaluation Pressure
comparativeKeyFindings.detail: Parsippany's assessments sit at 66.60% of true market value ($348.5k average assessment vs. ~$595k+ market value). As the ratio drops toward the 60% threshold, Morris County Tax Board scrutiny increases.
